cohort: A total of 100 pregnant females were enrolled and assigned into two groups based on their BMI (BMI <25 kg/m2 and BMI >=25 kg/m2) in a tertiary care centre.
finding: Maternal obesity significantly increases the risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including a longer hospital stay.
mod_finding: The rate of vaginal delivery was significantly lower in obese pregnant females (42%) compared to non-obese pregnant females (76%).
